Importing files and how recognition works

Which formats Diagram Studio reads, what each one preserves, how pictures and scanned PDFs are recognised, how to review doubtful items, and how to run and troubleshoot the import service.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsdiagrams.import diagrams.edit
📍 WhereDiagrams › Diagram Studio › Import (/diagram-studio/import)

What is it?#

The import wizard reads a file and rebuilds it as an editable SATOM diagram. Vector and structured formats (draw.io, Visio, SVG, PDF with a drawing, Mermaid, DOT) are converted: what the file says is what you get. Pictures and scanned pages are recognised: shapes, lines and text are inferred, each with a confidence, and anything doubtful is flagged for you to review before the diagram exists.

What does it do?#

Format Extensions How it is read Notes
draw.io / diagrams.net .drawio, .dio, .xml, draw.io-embedded .svg Exact, every page gradients (every direction and radial), shadows with their colour, fill and line opacity and dash patterns are kept; sketch style is dropped; shapes with no native equivalent become rectangles
Visio .vsdx (also .vsdm), .vdx Exact: shapes, masters, Shape Data, glued connectors two-stop gradients, shadows and dash / dot / dash-dot lines are kept; themes become flat colours, a gradient with more stops keeps its first and last, rectangular and path gradients are drawn radial (each noted in the warnings); curves and splines become straight lines; EMF/WMF pictures and background pages are skipped
Visio, legacy binary .vsd Not supported save it as .vsdx in Visio and import that
SVG .svg Exact geometry; connections inferred from where lines end linear and radial gradients (first and last stop), drop-shadow filters, opacities and dash arrays are kept; scripts, foreignObject, animations and external references are dropped and counted
PDF with a drawing .pdf Exact: the PDF's own drawing operators are read encrypted PDFs are refused; clipping, patterns and rotated text boxes are not interpreted
Scanned PDF .pdf Inferred: the page is rendered at 200 dpi and recognised like a picture needs Read text (OCR) ticked
Pictures .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .bmp, .tif, .tiff Inferred at most 50 megapixels and 64 MiB; a TIFF up to 20 pages
Mermaid .mmd, .mermaid parsed, then laid out by SATOM flowchart subset; the source has no coordinates
Graphviz DOT .dot, .gv parsed, then laid out by SATOM ports are ignored

Text recognition (OCR) runs offline on models shipped with SATOM and reads Latin script: English, Spanish, German, French, Italian and other Western European languages. Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew and CJK text is not recognised. Sharp, horizontal, high-contrast screenshots read well; low resolution, angled photographs and handwriting do not.

Requirements#

  • The diagrams.import permission (and diagrams.edit to accept the result).
  • The satom-diagrams service and its .path watcher enabled on the node that serves your session (both nodes of a pair).
  • bubblewrap installed on the node; without it nothing is parsed.

Permissions#

Operator and Administrator profiles hold diagrams.import; the read-only profile does not, and the Import page answers Forbidden. Every import, refusal and acceptance is written to the Audit Log as diagram.import, diagram.import_refused and diagram.import_accept.

How to use#

  1. 1Importchoose files, pages and options
  2. 2Recognitionone job per file: queued, running, ok / failed / refused
  3. 3Reviewcheck the flagged items, then Accept
  4. 4Editorthe diagram opens, version 1
  1. Open Diagrams › Diagram Studio › Import.
  2. Drop up to 20 files (50 MiB each) or browse. For a PDF, a TIFF or a multi-page draw.io or Visio file, choose the pages in the page picker (PDF pages show thumbnails; at most 50 PDF pages per import).
  3. Set the options: Read text (OCR) in pictures and scans and Classify elements (router, firewall, server...) are on by default; Refine with the local vision model is available only when an administrator configured one.
  4. Press Start recognition. Each file is a job. Refused means the file was turned away on purpose (unsupported, too large, legacy .vsd, encrypted PDF, a photo rather than a drawing, unsafe XML or ZIP): fix it and import it again. Failed means a reader crashed, timed out or hit the memory limit. The others continue either way, and Discard removes a job you do not want.
  5. In Review, check what is flagged (below) and press Accept. The diagram is created as version 1, noted Imported from , and the editor opens.

Review: what the marks mean#

Each mark is drawn on the canvas and listed in the side panel with an icon and a word, never by colour alone.

Mark Meaning
dashed amber outline low confidence (below 0.6): the shape or its text may be wrong
dotted violet outline unclassified: no category yet, typically an icon the classifier could not name
dotted line dangling connector: one end is not attached to a shape
amber halo with ! uncertain connector (below 0.6): its direction or an end may be wrong, typically an arrowhead that could not be read

For each flagged item you can set a category and a symbol (searchable pickers), correct its text, group or ungroup, or delete it. Any connector, flagged or not, can be clicked to pick its source and target again on the canvas, swap its direction or change its arrows. Edits are undoable. The classifier never invents: it labels an element only on evidence (the source's own hints, the label, the shape, its connectors), and an IP, CIDR, VLAN, ASN or hostname is recorded only when it parses as one. A category you set by hand is never overwritten.

Configuration#

Optional vision refinement#

A local, Ollama-compatible vision model can name icons and fix text that the recogniser was unsure about. It is off unless configured. An administrator sets both variables in the environment of the SATOM web service and restarts it:

Variable Meaning
SATOM_DIAGRAM_VISION_ENDPOINT an http or https URL of the model server, with no credentials in it
SATOM_DIAGRAM_VISION_MODEL the model name on that server

Both must be set. It applies to pictures and PDF pages only, and only fills the category and text of low-confidence elements; it never moves anything or adds elements. SATOM validates the reply strictly and rejects it entirely on any violation. The call is limited to 60 seconds. Without the settings, the wizard says Not configured on this console.

The service and its limits#

Item Value
Units satom-diagrams.path watches the queue; satom-diagrams.service is a one-shot unprivileged recogniser. Enabled on both nodes of a pair
Data /opt/satom/data/diagrams/ with queue, claimed, status, results, sources, rejected
Per recognition 180 seconds, inside the sandbox
Concurrency 2 recognitions at a time; up to 20 requests per service start
Caps MemoryMax=1G, TasksMax=256, CPUQuota=200% (raise them with a systemd drop-in for very large scans)
Retention status, results, sources and thumbnails older than 7 days are deleted; accepted diagrams are in the database

Example#

An engineer photographs a whiteboard and drops the JPEG on the wizard with OCR and classification ticked. Recognition finds eleven boxes and their links; Review flags two icons as unclassified and one connector as dangling. The engineer picks network.firewall for one icon, network.router for the other, clicks the missing target shape for the connector, and presses Accept.

Result#

A new diagram at version 1 in the library, with the source file's SHA-256 kept. Nothing from the upload remains on the node after 7 days except the diagram itself.

Imported symbols are classified to Flat icons. To give the drawing full colour or 3D icons, use Switch all to Colour or 3D in the editor (see Diagram Studio).

Troubleshooting#

"The recognition was killed: memory limit of satom-diagrams.service (MemoryMax) reached."#

Possible causes: the file is too large or too complex for the 1 GiB cap. Solution: import fewer pages, or a smaller or lower-resolution picture; an administrator can raise MemoryMax with a drop-in.

A job stays "queued"#

Possible causes: the watcher is not running (on a standby, the .path unit must be enabled too). Solution: check satom-diagrams.path and satom-diagrams.service with systemctl status and read the service's journal.

"Legacy binary Visio (.vsd) cannot be read; save it as .vsdx in Visio and import that."#

Open the file in Visio and use Save As .vsdx.

"The PDF is encrypted or password-protected"#

Remove the protection and import again.

"Page N is a scanned image"#

Tick Read text (OCR), or import the page as a PNG or JPEG.

"OCR is not available on this host; text was not read"#

The OCR runtime or its models could not be loaded. The models are checked against a SHA-256 manifest before every load; a missing or altered model is refused. The shapes are still imported, without text. Check that the Python dependencies of requirements.txt are installed and that the model files match the release.

"sandbox unavailable: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed"#

Install bubblewrap on the node.

"Diagram Studio is busy reading other files on this node; try again"#

The page picker and thumbnails are quick checks, two at a time per node. Wait a moment and retry.

"Vision refinement was not applied"#

The import still succeeded. Check that the endpoint answers, that the model exists on it and that it replies within 60 seconds.

Advanced#

Advanced How a file is kept safe

The web process stores the upload by its SHA-256 (mode 0600) and writes a request; it never parses. The satom-diagrams service runs each request in a sandbox with no network, no SATOM files, no database and no key. XML DOCTYPE and entity declarations are refused; ZIP containers are limited to 5 000 entries and a 200:1 compression ratio; SVG scripts and external references are stripped and reported once per kind. A request is moved to claimed before it runs, so a crash cannot replay it.
